cases.name: Alicia Lindsey Wood
cases.about: "She was probably the funniest girl I’ve ever met in my life. She had an incredible sense of humor and was incredibly smart," said (friend Gabrielle) Rosson. Rosson described Wood as a talented actor, writer, and poet with a passion for theater. "She studied at a theater school in New York... People in Montana probably don’t know that about her, but she was extremely intelligent, extremely funny, and extremely talented," she added.
cases.narrative:
Olson told officers that he and Wood had been arguing at her home when the dispute escalated and he killed her by strangling her in a headlock, according to the affidavit. He then allegedly placed Wood’s body inside a hard-sided suitcase he found in her closet and put it in the trunk of her car.

Olson allegedly told police he left the suitcase in a dumpster in Great Falls, near a local elementary school. According to the affidavit, sanitation trucks collected the trash from the dumpster on Nov. 27, and Wood’s body would have been offloaded at the landfill the following day.

The Cascade County Sheriff Office and several other agencies and volunteers have been searching the landfill, but no one has found Wood yet.
